title: Global-scale, verifiable mineral storage of carbon dioxide

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a repeatable way to store large quantities of carbon dioxide underground by converting it into solid minerals in reactive rock, while verifying how much conversion actually occurs. Success would require dependable performance across a range of geological settings, extending beyond favorable individual sites. Mineralization is already an active technology; the missing advance is globally deployable, verifiable performance.

Conceptual synthesis: The capability combines finding suitable reactive rock, bringing CO₂ into contact with it, sustaining fluid movement as minerals form, managing underground pressure and measuring the resulting carbon storage. Injection totals alone cannot establish the amount mineralized. Verification must distinguish carbon delivered underground from carbon shown to have become solid minerals, while accounting for carbon whose fate remains uncertain.

significance.text: Conditional significance: Reliable mineralization across many geological settings could substantially broaden access to durable geological carbon storage. The revolutionary step would be making storage performance predictable and repeatable across locations, with evidence that permits others to audit the amount stored. That would give storage planning a stronger basis than extrapolating from a small number of favorable demonstrations.

This advance would directly address the storage component of carbon management. Capturing CO₂, transporting it to a suitable site and reducing emissions remain separate requirements. Whether a particular project achieves net carbon removal would depend on where its CO₂ comes from and the emissions associated with its full operation. Successful underground mineralization alone would not establish net removal.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more locations able to host durable storage and more defensible carbon accounting for projects that use it. Those possibilities depend on acceptable water requirements, costs, operating reliability and environmental risks. Demonstrating rapid conversion at one site would not by itself establish climate-scale capacity, low costs or suitability in other rock formations.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability is sustained, verifiable mineralization at large scale across diverse geological settings. The supplied research identifies a central engineering tension: reactive rock must remain accessible to CO₂-bearing fluids even as mineral precipitation can reduce the permeability needed to reach more rock. An operational breakthrough must sustain useful contact and flow over time, rather than merely demonstrate that a rock can react.

Water demand, injectivity and pressure management are additional barriers identified in the supplied research. A useful system would need to avoid impractical freshwater requirements while maintaining injection performance and controlling leakage and seismic risks. The supplied review did not have retained source text with which to establish the magnitude or severity of these constraints, so their site-specific importance and acceptable operating limits remain open.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: Verification must connect observations from a limited set of wells and monitored flow paths to a defensible carbon balance for the storage operation. It must separate measured quantities, tracer-based inferences and extrapolations, and quantify uncertainty in carbon that has not been located or characterized. Geological characterization, geochemistry, hydrology and reservoir engineering must therefore work together with carbon accounting.

current_state.text: The supplied research attributes an important pilot result to the 2024 review, “Carbon Mineralization in Fractured Mafic and Ultramafic Rocks”: tracer-based analysis at CarbFix1 inferred that more than 95% of the injected dissolved CO₂ mineralized along the monitored flow path within two years. This is a reported inference with a defined monitoring scope, rather than a direct measurement of every part of the reservoir. The supplied material does not establish equivalent conversion throughout an entire storage formation or across other sites.

The research also reports that the same review describes larger cumulative injection at CarbFix2. No injection quantity, operating interval or corresponding mineralized fraction is supplied here. Larger cumulative injection and verified mineral conversion are different achievements; the former cannot establish the latter without additional evidence. Neither the reported CarbFix1 inference nor the CarbFix2 injection history establishes globally repeatable, low-cost mineralization at climate-relevant scale.

These findings must be read with an evidence-access limitation. The supplied source index contains the review’s title and DOI but no retained document, extracted text or other source artifact. The accompanying assessment therefore could not inspect the cited sections 2.2.3–2.2.4 or Figure 2, confirm the quantitative claims, or assess document completeness. The research notes a 2024 correction to the article, but its content and effect are not supplied. These limitations leave the reported findings unverified within this record; they do not demonstrate that the findings are false.

Temporal limitation: No bounded search record or later evidence was supplied, so this record cannot assess developments through November 1, 2026. The two-year figure describes the reported pilot’s conversion interval; it does not date the experiment. The available material supports describing a reported pilot achievement and subsequent injection activity, with unresolved questions about scale, transferability and practical performance.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Independently monitored sites in different rock types and geological settings should sustain substantial mineralization over an explicitly defined operating period. A convincing program would specify in advance what counts as large scale, how long performance must persist and what constitutes successful replication. These would be proposed evaluation thresholds, not established standards. A finite collection of successful sites would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested settings, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed verification: Each site should provide an auditable carbon mass balance that distinguishes injected carbon, carbon inferred or measured to be mineralized, other stored carbon and unresolved quantities. Monitoring methods, assumptions, uncertainty estimates and the spatial reach of observations should be available for independent scrutiny. Replication should test whether the measurement and inference methods remain reliable under different flow conditions and geological structures.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed verification

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: Demonstrations should report lifecycle emissions, water use and water source, costs, injection performance, pressure management, leakage observations and seismic monitoring. Acceptance limits should be declared and justified for the intended application. Sustained performance should show whether mineral precipitation progressively restricts access to reactive rock and whether maintaining operation remains practical.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed interpretation: Completion should include a clear account of where the method works, where it fails and which conditions control that boundary. Evidence for durable mineral storage should be assessed separately from claims about capture, transport or net carbon removal. Broader deployment claims would require capacity and resource assessments beyond successful site demonstrations.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed interpretation

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: GEO-03, “Geothermal reservoirs engineered economically in ordinary deep rock,” has the closest engineering overlap through subsurface access, permeability, fluid circulation and pressure management. Its objective is useful heat extraction; GEO-04 aims to convert and retain carbon in minerals. Mineral precipitation may constrain fluid access in GEO-04, making its reaction and flow requirements distinct from those of an engineered geothermal reservoir.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-01, “Reliable short-term forecasting of damaging earthquakes,” and GEO-10, “Reliable transferable forecasting of volcanic eruptions,” share questions about interpreting subsurface observations and establishing predictive reliability across sites. Seismic risk management is relevant to GEO-04, but reliable storage does not require solving general earthquake or eruption forecasting. Their forecasting objectives remain separate from storage verification.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-06, “Discovery of globally consequential recoverable geological hydrogen,” overlaps in geological resource characterization and the need to establish practical performance beyond a promising occurrence. It concerns finding and recovering an energy resource; GEO-04 concerns placing carbon underground and verifying its conversion and retention. Neither capability establishes the other.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-02, “A chemically and thermally resolved map of Earth’s deep interior,” GEO-05, “Recovery of a detailed geological record of Earth’s first half-billion years,” GEO-07, “Reconstructing the Moon-forming impact from independent geological evidence,” and GEO-08, “Establishing when and how sustained plate tectonics began,” share an interest in geological composition, reactions or inference from incomplete observations. Their targets are deep-Earth structure and planetary history; GEO-04 requires operational characterization and monitoring of particular storage formations.

Roster-based synthesis: GEO-09, “Predictive laws linking erosion, sediment transport and landscape evolution,” shares the ambition to develop explanations that transfer across settings. Its focus is surface processes and landscape change, whereas GEO-04 concerns subsurface reactive flow and carbon storage. Transferability is a common scientific challenge, not evidence that either innovation subsumes the other.

unresolved_issues: The source document and cited passages were not retained, so the CarbFix1 quantitative inference and its precise observational scope remain unverified within the supplied evidence.
The CarbFix2 cumulative injection quantity, operating dates and independently supported mineralized fraction are not supplied.
The content of the article’s reported 2024 correction and whether it affects any relevant claim remain unknown.
The site-specific magnitude of permeability loss, water requirements, leakage risk and seismic risk cannot be established from the supplied source metadata.
Operational definitions of large scale, sustained duration, acceptable cost, resource use and risk remain to be specified.
No supplied search record establishes developments through November 1, 2026; this record cannot determine the latest state of deployment.
